text: The ingredients at Parker’s seem decent, but the whole experience feels seriously overpriced for what you actually get. • Kale salad: Barely anything but kale. Very plain, feels more like a garnish than a proper salad, especially at their price point. • Truffle pasta: Genuinely delicious – rich, flavorful, and the highlight of the meal. We asked for extra chicken, but they added so little it felt more symbolic than actual “extra.” • Dessert (“pull me” cake): More of a social-media show than a good dessert. Overly sweet and not as tasty as the dramatic presentation suggests – it’s mainly for recording a video, not for enjoying every bite. • Coffee: Not great in terms of taste/beans, but it is at least prepared well. Technically fine, just not memorable. • Service & ambience: Service is okay – functional but not warm or special. The plates and cutlery are fancy and look premium, but we didn’t come here to eat those. That polish doesn’t fully compensate for the underwhelming food value. Overall, Parker’s looks upscale and tries to impress with presentation and “Instagram moments,” but when you factor in price versus what’s on the plate, it feels overvalued.
